name: human and organisational
owns: the people and processes that hold the same authority as the code: support desks, employees, contractors, onboarding, incident response and the workflows built around them
why_in_D: Every control in the other fifteen lenses can be walked around by asking a person. A support agent with a reset button is a more reliable path than any injection. An organisation that cannot tell which of its own processes touches a credential has an attack surface made of people, and it is the only lens where the attacker's cheapest option is conversation.

factors.name: support identity verification strength
factors.def: what a support agent requires before acting on an account, and whether it is knowledge based
factors.observable: an account action performed from public information alone

factors.name: reset authority scope
factors.def: whether one agent can reset credentials without a second approval
factors.observable: a reset completed by a single actor

factors.name: caller identification trust
factors.def: whether the channel itself (phone number, email address) is treated as proof of identity
factors.observable: an action taken on the basis of the channel alone

factors.name: voice cloning viability
factors.def: whether an authorisation depends on recognising a voice
factors.observable: an approval obtained from a synthetic voice

factors.name: urgency and pressure response
factors.def: whether process has an exception for urgency that skips verification
factors.observable: a skipped check justified by escalation

factors.name: authority impersonation surface
factors.def: how much a claimed role (executive, auditor, regulator) changes behaviour
factors.observable: an action taken because of a claimed title

factors.name: third party vendor trust
factors.def: whether being a known supplier reduces verification for account changes
factors.observable: a payment or credential change accepted on supplier status

factors.name: onboarding credential handover
factors.def: how a new employee receives their first credential and who can read it in transit
factors.observable: an initial password visible to a third party

factors.name: offboarding completeness
factors.def: what survives a departure: accounts, tokens, local files, device trust, shared passwords
factors.observable: an access path still working after the last day

factors.name: shared account usage
factors.def: whether accounts are personal or shared, which decides attribution
factors.observable: an action that cannot be attributed to one person

factors.name: password manager coverage
factors.def: whether credentials are in a manager or in notes, chat and spreadsheets
factors.observable: a credential found outside the manager

factors.name: mfa fatigue and push bombing
factors.def: whether repeated prompts can be worn down into an approval
factors.observable: an approval after a burst of prompts

factors.name: phishing resistant factor coverage
factors.def: which accounts still rely on a factor that a proxy can relay
factors.observable: a login completed through a reverse proxy with a real factor

factors.name: device trust enrollment path
factors.def: whether a device can be enrolled from outside a managed process
factors.observable: an unmanaged device treated as trusted

factors.name: personal device boundary
factors.def: what organisational data reaches a personal device and whether it can be removed
factors.observable: work data on a device outside management

factors.name: chat and collaboration data gravity
factors.def: what credentials, links and internal detail have been pasted into chat
factors.observable: a credential in message history

factors.name: screenshot and screen share leakage
factors.def: what is visible in a shared screen during a call, and what is recorded
factors.observable: a secret on screen in a recorded session

factors.name: insider data movement baseline
factors.def: whether there is a baseline for normal access volume, without which exfiltration is invisible
factors.observable: a bulk read with no alert

factors.name: privileged access approval trail
factors.def: whether elevated access is requested, approved and recorded
factors.observable: an elevated session with no approval record

factors.name: break glass credential custody
factors.def: where emergency credentials are kept and who can reach them
factors.observable: an emergency credential available without a second party

factors.name: production access breadth
factors.def: how many people can read production data directly
factors.observable: a person with direct production read access

factors.name: customer data in test environments
factors.def: whether real data reaches lower environments where controls are lighter
factors.observable: a real record in a test store

factors.name: incident response decision authority
factors.def: who can shut a service down, and whether the answer is a person or a committee
factors.observable: delay between detection and a reversible action

factors.name: runbook accuracy
factors.def: whether the documented recovery path matches the system as built
factors.observable: a runbook step that no longer exists

factors.name: escalation path reachability
factors.def: whether a report reaches someone who can act, out of hours
factors.observable: time to a human acknowledgement

factors.name: disclosure handling
factors.def: whether an external report is acknowledged, triaged and rewarded, or ignored
factors.observable: an unacknowledged report older than the stated window

factors.name: bug bounty scope definition
factors.def: whether scope is precise enough that researchers test the real system rather than the wrong one
factors.observable: a report marked out of scope for a real issue

factors.name: safe harbour clarity
factors.def: whether good faith testing is protected in writing
factors.observable: an ambiguous policy that discourages reporting

factors.name: security training effectiveness
factors.def: whether training changes behaviour or only records completion
factors.observable: click rate on a simulated lure after training

factors.name: developer security feedback loop
factors.def: whether a developer learns that their change introduced a weakness, and how fast
factors.observable: repeat rate of the same class of mistake

factors.name: review depth on security relevant changes
factors.def: whether auth, payment and crypto changes get a different review than a typo fix
factors.observable: an auth change merged with one approval

factors.name: code ownership coverage
factors.def: whether every sensitive path has a named owner who would notice a change
factors.observable: a sensitive file with no owner

factors.name: contractor and agency access
factors.def: whether external workers get the same lifecycle and the same review
factors.observable: an external account without an expiry

factors.name: acquisition and merger inheritance
factors.def: whether an acquired system's identities and credentials were ever merged or retired
factors.observable: an account from before an acquisition still active

factors.name: regulatory notification obligation
factors.def: whether the organisation knows its reporting deadlines and who decides to notify
factors.observable: a breach with no recorded notification decision

factors.name: law enforcement and legal access path
factors.def: what a legal request can obtain, and whether that path is authenticated
factors.observable: a data release without a verification step

factors.name: customer support data visibility
factors.def: what an agent can see beyond the ticket, which is often the whole account
factors.observable: a support view exposing fields unrelated to the request

factors.name: internal tooling authentication
factors.def: whether internal dashboards are protected by the same policy as external ones
factors.observable: an internal tool reachable with weaker authentication

factors.name: api key sharing in integrations
factors.def: whether a key is shared between people or systems, which removes attribution
factors.observable: one key used by several distinct clients

factors.name: handover documentation completeness
factors.def: whether the knowledge to operate a system leaves with the person who built it
factors.observable: a system nobody remaining can safely change

factors.name: security team authority
factors.def: whether security can block a release or is advisory only
factors.observable: a release shipped against a security objection

factors.name: metrics that incentivise the wrong behaviour
factors.def: whether a target (close tickets, ship fast) creates pressure to bypass a control
factors.observable: a control bypassed to meet a number

factors.name: exception register
factors.def: whether accepted risks are recorded with an owner and an expiry
factors.observable: an exception with no end date

factors.name: third party risk assessment depth
factors.def: whether a supplier's security was assessed on evidence or on a questionnaire
factors.observable: a supplier with unaudited access to data

factors.name: vendor access to production
factors.def: whether a supplier has standing access and whether it is logged like an employee
factors.observable: a vendor session missing from the audit trail

factors.name: supply of hardware and devices
factors.def: whether devices arrive through a controlled channel and are inspected
factors.observable: a device enrolled without provenance

factors.name: physical access to infrastructure
factors.def: who can touch a server, a network port or a console
factors.observable: a physical action with no record

factors.name: tailgating and badge policy
factors.def: whether physical entry is challenged or assumed
factors.observable: entry without a check

factors.name: paper and whiteboard residue
factors.def: what credentials and architecture exist outside any system
factors.observable: a secret written where it can be photographed

factors.name: conference and public speaking leakage
factors.def: whether a talk or post revealed architecture, credentials or unreleased detail
factors.observable: operational detail in a public recording

factors.name: recruitment and job posting leakage
factors.def: what a job advert reveals about internal stack and versions
factors.observable: specific internal technology named publicly

factors.name: social media operational leakage
factors.def: whether staff posts reveal access, schedules or systems
factors.observable: operational detail in a personal post

factors.name: phishing domain registration monitoring
factors.def: whether lookalike domains for the brand are watched
factors.observable: a registered lookalike nobody noticed

factors.name: credential leak monitoring
factors.def: whether staff credentials appearing in public dumps are detected and rotated
factors.observable: a valid staff credential in a public corpus

factors.name: customer education accuracy
factors.def: whether users are told what the organisation will never ask for, and whether that is true
factors.observable: a legitimate contact that matches the warning pattern

factors.name: fraud team integration
factors.def: whether abuse and fraud signals reach the security team and vice versa
factors.observable: an abuse pattern known to one team and not the other

factors.name: legal hold versus deletion conflict
factors.def: whether a deletion obligation conflicts with a preservation order and who resolves it
factors.observable: data retained past a stated deadline

factors.name: insider threat detection coverage
factors.def: whether anomalous internal behaviour is detectable at all
factors.observable: an unusual bulk access with no signal

factors.name: whistleblower and reporting channel
factors.def: whether someone who notices something wrong has a route that does not cost them their job
factors.observable: an internal concern with no channel

factors.name: post incident change rate
factors.def: whether a root cause produces a durable change or a document
factors.observable: the same incident class recurring

factors.name: assumption of shared context
factors.def: whether an instruction assumes the reader knows something only the author knows, which is how a bypass becomes normal
factors.observable: a step in a runbook that depends on unrecorded knowledge

factors.name: authority gradient in reporting
factors.def: whether a junior can escalate past a senior who is wrong
factors.observable: a correct concern suppressed by seniority
